title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Work, an AI Agent That Manages Email, Slack, and Calendars Across Your Office
excerpt: Powered by the new GPT-5.6 model, the agentic platform can create documents, presentations, and websites autonomously — marking OpenAI's biggest push into enterprise territory.
body:
• OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work, a cloud-based AI agent that can manage tasks across email, Slack, calendars, CRMs, and other business tools — going beyond chat to actually execute multi-step workflows.
  • Powered by the newly released GPT-5.6 model (delayed last month over US government national security concerns), the platform can autonomously create documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and web apps.
  • ChatGPT Work directly competes with Anthropic's Claude Cowork and Microsoft's Copilot Cowork, as all three race to build autonomous workplace agents for enterprise customers.
  • Available to Plus subscribers at $20/month, OpenAI is leveraging its 900 million weekly active user base to undercut competitors on accessibility and price.

From Chatbot to Office Agent

OpenAI took its most significant step yet toward making ChatGPT a workplace tool rather than just a conversational assistant, launching ChatGPT Work — an agentic platform that can plan, execute, and deliver complex business tasks across connected office systems.

Built on OpenAI's Codex technology, ChatGPT Work connects to workplace tools via plugins — Slack, Google Drive, email systems, calendars, CRMs, and project management platforms. Once connected, it can retrieve information, create drafts, refine documents, build spreadsheets and presentations, and carry out longer-running tasks that previously required human coordination across multiple applications.

"You can apply the model's ability to code to solve problems across every industry," said Ty Geri, product manager for ChatGPT Work. He described the underlying GPT-5.6 model as "competitive with models that are far, far more expensive at twice the speed and much, much cheaper."

Three-Way Race for the Enterprise

ChatGPT Work drops into what has become the defining competitive battleground in AI: the race to build autonomous workplace agents that can go beyond generating text and actually get things done.

The product arrives months after Anthropic took Claude Cowork out of preview and into general availability in April, and after Microsoft made Copilot Cowork available globally on June 16. All three products share a remarkably similar vision: a persistent AI agent running in the cloud that breaks complex tasks into steps, connects to workplace tools, and produces finished outputs rather than conversational replies.

What distinguishes OpenAI's approach is raw distribution. ChatGPT has reached 900 million weekly active users, with 50 million paying subscribers and more than 9 million paying business users. By making ChatGPT Work available to Plus subscribers at $20 per month — not just Enterprise or Pro customers — OpenAI is betting that broad accessibility will drive adoption faster than any competitor can match.

"The result is stronger performance per dollar: more successful work for the same spend, or comparable results at a lower total cost."

— OpenAI, on GPT-5.6's design philosophy

GPT-5.6: Delayed, Now Deployed

The launch also marks the broader rollout of GPT-5.6, OpenAI's most advanced model. The release was delayed last month at the US government's request over national security concerns related to advanced cybersecurity and biology capabilities.

OpenAI is pitching GPT-5.6 not on raw benchmark superiority but on performance per dollar — a shift from its traditional messaging. The company released three model sizes: Sol (the flagship, priced at $5 per million input tokens and $30 per million output tokens), Terra, and Luna, with progressively lower-cost options for organisations scaling AI deployments.

What It Means for India's Tech Workforce

For India's millions of IT professionals and knowledge workers, ChatGPT Work represents both opportunity and disruption. The tool's ability to automate document creation, data analysis, report generation, and cross-platform coordination touches directly on tasks performed by business analysts, project coordinators, and junior associates across India's IT services sector.

Companies like Nvidia, Zapier, RingCentral, and Virgin Atlantic have been using ChatGPT Work in beta testing. Internal use cases at OpenAI include transforming customer discovery notes into a proof of concept within 24 hours and reducing month-end financial close from days to hours — precisely the kind of efficiency gains that Indian IT companies both deliver to clients and will need to achieve internally.

The enterprise AI agent market is moving fast. For India's technology sector, the question is whether firms can ride this wave as implementers and service providers, or whether the automation these tools enable will compress the very roles that sustain the industry's workforce.
